message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001299","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates match the target endpoint (cervical carcinoma/cervical cancer), so performance evidence and comparability drive the choice (prs_model_evaluator skill_overview; performance_metrics section). PGS001299 is the only candidate reporting clearly PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.552 and PGS-only R²=0.00263), plus incremental AUROC, which makes its standalone genetic contribution interpretable; most other candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index with nontrivial covariate sets, which is not reliably comparable across models. Although PGS000073/PGS000784 show higher full-model AUROC (~0.745), those are likely substantially covariate-driven (age, parity, oral contraceptive use, smoking), and they do not provide PRS-only discrimination to rank the PGS itself. Heritability lookup for 'cervical cancer' returned a UKBB self-reported cervical cancer h2≈0.00011 observed (liability ≈0.0020), suggesting low detectable SNP-heritability in that specific phenotype definition; this supports interpreting the modest PRS-only R² from PGS001299 as plausible and not obviously inconsistent with an h2 ceiling, while treating high full-model AUROCs as potentially non-genetic/covariate-driven (performance_metrics heritability sanity-check guidance)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002037","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity is good for both candidates: trait_efo matches the target (nicotine dependence) and the reported/phenotyped label is the close synonym “Tobacco use disorder.” Per prs_model_evaluator guidance on interpreting performance evidence (read_skill_section: performance_metrics), when PRS-only AUC/R2 are missing for all candidates, small differences in reported metrics are not decisive and structural signals (method, variant count) become the more reliable tie-breakers. Both models come from the same UKB portability framework with similar training N (391,124), validation N (19,400 Europeans), and basic covariates, so the main differentiators are method and the available PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation). PGS002037 (LDpred2) shows higher partial-r (0.0741 vs 0.0557) and uses a much denser genome-wide variant set (847,691 vs 13,838), which is typically favorable within the same study context. Heritability sanity-check was attempted via get_heritability_records for both “nicotine dependence” and the close label “tobacco use disorder,” but no matching EUR h2 records were returned, so h2 could not be used to contextualize the partial-r magnitude; confidence is therefore Moderate rather than High."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000082","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Trait match: target is ovarian neoplasm; PGS000082 is directly aligned to ovarian cancer (trait_efo ovarian carcinoma) with incident ovarian cancer phenotyping, which is a close match to malignant ovarian neoplasm. Several other candidates are BRCA-carrier–specific (e.g., PGS000048/PGS000351/PGS002250) or subtype-specific (serous/high-grade serous), which are less general for the broad target.

Evidence strength and comparability: Per the performance-metrics guidance (prs_model_evaluator skill section: performance_metrics), most candidates only report full-model AUROC/C-index (not PGS-only), so small AUROC differences are not decisive and covariate sets matter. PGS000082 has the strongest combination of (i) large-scale evaluation (n=211,958; EUR), (ii) disease-focused cross-cancer evaluation context, and (iii) the best reported full-model discrimination among broadly matched, general-population ovarian cancer scores in the list (AUROC ~0.656 / C-index ~0.655). Although covariates are extensive (age, family history, reproductive/hormonal factors, PCs, etc.), this is still the most robustly evaluated general ovarian cancer PRS here.

Why not the PRSweb ‘ovarian neoplasm’ scores (PGS000544–PGS000564): they match the EFO label exactly, but their reported discrimination is consistently weak (AUROC ~0.52–0.57; pseudo-R² mostly ~0.002–0.011) in relatively small evaluations (~5,196), suggesting limited utility despite exact label match.

Heritability sanity check: get_heritability_records("ovarian neoplasm") returned no matches; a broader lookup for "ovarian cancer" returned only non-cancer ovarian conditions (ovarian cyst/PCOS) with low observed h2 and nonzero liability-scale h2, so these h2 records are not directly informative for malignant ovarian neoplasm PRS performance and are used only as a caution against over-interpreting any single metric."}
